title: Traffic sizing and script adaptation POC kickoff
next_steps: Redwood to share POC runbook and harness adapter spec by EOD 2026-06-29
Brightleaf to send representative sample of production scripts and 2 weeks of traffic profiles by 2026-07-02
Schedule engineering sync to validate KV-cache warmup plan w/ latency slices on 2026-07-06
action_items: Sofia Martin: Send POC runbook + harness adapter spec (due 2026-06-29)
Priya Nair: Export and upload anonymized client scripts + traffic CSV (due 2026-07-02)
Daniel Cho: Draft streaming vs non-streaming benchmark matrix and expected failure modes (due 2026-07-03)
summary: Kickoff to scope POC for benchmark harness integration. Focus: sizing traffic, mapping customer scripts to Redwood harness, decision criteria for streaming vs non-streaming, and success criteria for throughput/latency. Action items agreed to share artifacts and schedule a technical run next week.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~57 minutes | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Asha (Redwood SE), Michael (Brightleaf Head of ML), Priya (Platform Eng), Jules (SRE), Anita (Product)

0:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, thank you for joining. quick intro round, we'll keep this focused — objective is to scope the POC harness integration and decide on streaming vs non-streaming approach.
0:18 Michael: Thanks, Sofia. We're excited. quick context — Brightleaf runs a real-time analytics assistant on top of several open models, we currently host inference on-prem with a mix of A100s and some older cards. main pain is unpredictable tail latency and cost spikes.
0:36 Daniel: got it. and the POC goals roughly are validating throughput at your peak 95th percentile, confirming prefix/KV cache warmup behavior, and measuring cost per 1k tokens for both streaming and non-streaming flows, is that fair?
0:54 Michael: yes. and we also need clear success criteria for the execs — they want to see parity or better latencies at 40% lower unit cost, and no regression on accuracy metrics for our reranking stage.
1:12 Priya: to add, our infra constraints: traffic goes through an internal router, we have TLS termination at edge, and some requests include PII so we require private VPC deployment for the pilot. is Redwood okay with that?
1:30 Sofia: absolutely, Redwood Private is the intended mode here. For the harness we can run the controller in your VPC and we only need outbound for telemetry if you opt in — we can also run fully air-gapped if needed but that'll add time.
1:48 Jules: timeline question — we have a tight Q3 deadline for launch. what's realistic for a benchmark POC?
2:00 Asha: typical timeline is 2–3 weeks for harness adapter and baseline runs, assuming customer provides scripts and traffic profiles in the first 72 hours. then 1 week for iterative tuning. so roughly 3–4 weeks end-to-end.
2:18 Michael: okay. let me walk through our workload: most requests are short summaries (avg 120 tokens) but we have a 5% heavy path with multi-turn context ~1,200 tokens and a reranking step that adds an extra generation call. peak concurrency is ~650 concurrent requests across services with bursts to 1,000.
2:36 Daniel: that's useful. for sizing we'll map that to token/sec and effective batch sizes. do you currently do streaming token-by-token to clients or buffer?
2:52 Michael: we stream partials to the UI for chat, but the reranker is non-streaming. some internal pipelines expect immediate finalized output.
3:10 Sofia: so we need to benchmark both streaming and non-streaming flows, and measure end-to-end user-visible latency for streaming (time-to-first-byte and time-to-last-byte) plus backend tail for non-streaming.
3:26 Priya: our scripts are a mix of internal python wrappers that call an in-house SDK; we can extract representative calls. would Redwood prefer a particular harness format?
3:40 Daniel: we accept customer scripts as simple HTTP call records or as adapter code in a small shim. preferred is a replayable JSON lines format with request payload, timestamps, and optional client-side timing. we'll share an adapter example.
3:56 Priya: ok we'll extract to that format. one tricky bit: our SDK does optimistic batching client-side which adds jitter — how do you account for that?
4:12 Asha: we'll emulate client batching in the harness (configurable inter-arrival distributions). good to capture both your real client jitter and a synthetic Poisson baseline.
4:28 Jules: about KV cache warmup — in prod we see cold-start optouts when a model variant spins up, some sessions show 2–3x latency for first few tokens. how will that be modeled in the POC?
4:46 Daniel: we can seed the KV cache by replaying warmup traffic prior to the measured run. harness supports staged runs: cold, warmed, sustained. we'll define warmup windows that match your session affinity patterns.
5:04 Michael: nice. can you also simulate the rerank call chain — first generation, then scoring with a separate model? that's a critical path for us.
5:18 Asha: yes, we can chain calls in the harness and measure compound latency. we'll also measure token-level cost across both calls and quantify savings if you run lighter quantized variants for the reranker.
5:34 Priya: speaking of quantization — we are evaluating int8 MQA variants; will that affect the streaming path?
5:44 Daniel: streaming behavior is mostly independent of quantization, but quantization can change per-token latency; we'll include model variant runs in the matrix.
5:58 Anita: success criteria from product side: 95th percentile end-to-end latency under 600ms for chat short paths, reranker p95 under 900ms, and token-cost reduction at or above 30% versus current. are those realistic?
6:18 Sofia: they are reasonable targets to test. we'll capture metrics and present a summary dashboard. acceptance will be based on agreed test cases — we'll need a handful of canonical prompts and rerank sets.
6:34 Michael: we'll provide those. on security compliance: SOC2 reports and SSO/SAML are required to proceed. do you have SAML integrations for the console?
6:44 Sofia: yes, Redwood supports SAML SSO and we can provide SOC2 Type II. for the Private deployment we'll work with your security team on audit log detail.
7:00 Priya: great. one more: telemetry sampling and PII — can we redact certain fields before telemetry leaves our VPC?
7:10 Asha: yes, we support local redaction hooks and only surface aggregate telemetry by default. sensitive payloads can be omitted from logs.
7:20 Jules: operational question — if the dedicated pool saturates, will Redwood automatically route to a fallback model variant or region? we need graceful degradation.
7:32 Daniel: yes, routing policies can fail over to a cheaper or lower-capacity variant; we can configure canary and fallback with traffic split rules. we'll show a runbook for scaling and fallback.
7:46 Michael: ok good. let's talk concrete numbers for the benchmark matrix: what dimensions do you need?
7:54 Daniel: model variant, streaming vs non-streaming, cold vs warmed, concurrency slices (100, 350, 650, 1000), batching config, and input length buckets (short/medium/heavy). we'll output p50/p95/p99 latencies, token/sec, GPU utilization and estimated cost per 1k tokens.
8:22 Priya: can you include power/cost extrapolation for our on-prem cluster vs Redwood Private? execs will want TCO numbers.
8:32 Sofia: yes we'll include a cost model. it'll be approximate but useful for decisioning.
8:40 Michael: regarding instrumentation — we use OpenTelemetry and already export traces. can Redwood ingest our traces or should we push logs to a shared S3?
8:52 Daniel: OpenTelemetry traces are ideal; we can ingest them if you provide endpoint access or ship them to a preconfigured collector in your VPC. logs artifacts can be S3 or local retention.
9:04 Priya: perfect. next, acceptance criteria and sign-off: who signs off on the POC?
9:12 Sofia: suggested: Michael (ML lead) signs off on accuracy and latency metrics, Jules signs off on ops and reliability, and Priya on security/infra. we'll include a final report and a demo walkthrough.
9:28 Michael: sounds good. any blockers?
9:32 Priya: principal blocker is getting scripts and traffic export in anonymized form — will need to coordinate with legal for PII redaction.
9:42 Sofia: understood. we'll wait for the artifacts; meanwhile we'll send the harness spec and a sample adapter repo.
9:50 Anita: can we also get a simple checklist for what success looks like? execs prefer a 1‑page summary.
9:58 Sofia: yes, one-pager with pass/fail gates per success criteria — we'll draft it.
10:06 Daniel: quick technical note: for streaming tests measured metrics include time-to-first-byte and stream throughput; we sometimes see client-side reassembly issues when chunk sizes differ — recommend we validate with your UI team during the run.
10:24 Michael: we'll loop in the frontend folks.
10:28 Priya: final question — do you support replaying auth headers or should we sanitize them?
10:34 Asha: do not include real auth tokens; use placeholders and the harness can sign calls with a test key.
10:40 Sofia: ok recap of next steps: Redwood sends runbook + adapter spec (Sofia), Brightleaf to provide scripts and traffic (Priya), Redwood drafts benchmark matrix and run schedule (Daniel). goal to run first warmed baseline by 2026-07-09.
10:58 Michael: thanks all. we'll aim to get artifacts to you by end of week.
11:06 Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
11:12 Meeting end.
